attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'as far as I can tell' qualifier and both clauses: the White House taking cues from podcasts, and the podcasters refusing his rebuttal. It is an observation, but the influence clause is a hedged inference. The refusal clause is a separate factual allegation.

contract.note: The contract does not grade the hedged influence inference as a flat assertion, which is fair. A result would depend on how far the hedge reaches and on splitting the two clauses, neither of which Marcus specified. Even scored alone, the refusal clause would need communications that the packet does not contain.

evidence.note: A secondary summary from July 2025 reporting that Vance read AI 2027 but did not listen to Douthat's podcast. Douthat's show is not one of the podcasts Marcus named. The item says nothing about the refusals or about influence from All-In, Dwarkesh, Lex or Hard Fork.

reviews.rationale: The influence clause is Marcus's expressly hedged inference, so it is not scored. The combined statement cannot get one factual grade without removing the hedge or scoring only part of it. The refusal clause could in principle be checked, but the packet has no communications or host acknowledgments, so it would be unresolved anyway. The one evidence item (e1) is context only.
